facts.value: Western Digital Corporation (WDC), through its wholly-owned subsidiary Lodi Ventures, Inc.
Strategic: developer and manufacturer of storage products
DEFM14A definitive proxy statement, dated 08/07/2013, filed 08/08/2013
Activist-influenced: Balch Hill letter urging exploration of strategic alternatives (#4) precedes round 1

Informal, exploratory approaches over prior years with no terms proposed; 2011 lunch at which WDC CEO John Coyne noted interest in expanding in SSDs; summer 2012 lunch at which WDC's Michael Hajeck asked about the Moshayedis' plans.
Met (process 1): 6 parties (WDC, Companies D, E, F, G, H)

facts.field: Currency and units of bid prices

facts.value: Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP (outside corporate counsel); Latham & Watkins LLP (litigation counsel to sTec and Manouch Moshayedi)

Facing losses and activist pressure from Balch Hill, sTec's board began a strategic review in November 2012 and formed a special committee in February 2013. After hiring BofA Merrill Lynch, it approached 18 prospective acquirers from April 2013; six signed NDAs, and WDC, Company D and Company H submitted indications of $6.60–$7.10, $5.75 and $5.00–$5.75. WDC and Company D were invited to a final round; WDC bid $9.15 with a merger agreement mark-up and confirmed it as best and final, while Company D repeatedly asked for more time. The day after the board chose WDC, WDC said it was not prepared to proceed; Company D disengaged on 06/05/2013. WDC returned with a $6.60–$7.10 range, and when the board demanded a single best price it offered $6.85. The merger agreement was signed on 06/23/2013 at $6.85 per share in cash and announced the next day.
